notes.title: A Message to the notmycar Community
notes.content:
We hoped this day would never come, but here we are. After 2 1/2 years of long nights and weekends trying to get notmycar off the ground, we have decided to shut down the servers as of midnight on 9/30. It was a difficult decision, but one that we feel is right for us at this time. We had big plans for the game, including taking it to console and adding new game modes, but unfortunately we weren't able to secure the investment to do so. FYI, making games is hard, and making money making games is even harder. 

We are greatly appreciative of all of the support and love we've received from the community since the game launched - especially those of you who were with us from the very beginning. To the Content Crew and Auto Club - thanks for your additional support taking screenshots, capturing video, and in general helping us test and tune the game. We had loads of fun working with you. To those of you who showed up to our playdates, even when they were scheduled at the last minute and weren't super friendly to EU timezones - THANK YOU!! It was a pleasure dropping into battle with you. And extra special thanks to Greenskull and Potts for organizing the community, working with marketing, handling our social accounts, and in generally helping to evangelize the game - your contribution was invaluable - our community would not have existed without you. In addition to our players, we’d like to thank our partners at Skybound, Valve, Alienware, Razer, and Twitch for supporting us these last 2 years. And last but not least, thanks to our awesome art outsourcing partner, ArtBully, for helping us with this project. You guys are the best.

So, with this being the final weekend, we'd like to invite all of you to one last playdate with the developers before we close up shop. [b]We'll be on from 4-6pm Friday, 9/27[/b], and then intermittently throughout the weekend. Look for us in our black and gold developer buggies, and join us in discord! As an added bonus, [b]we're lowering all of the prices in the store to FREE![/b] We will also be offering refunds to anyone who purchased an item since the start of Season 2 - please [url=https://discord.gg/notmycar]message us directly in our Discord[/url] and we'll get you taken care of. 

Well, that's it then. We hope you enjoyed your time playing notmycar - see you on the battlefield! 

<3 Turbo Racington

notes.title: 7.19.19 Update - notmycar Season 2 is coming in hot!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34046600/0855e91bc13596552a98c5c5eac51de7f4888176.png[/img]

It's official: after months of work, we're proud to announce that notmycar Season 2 is launching for free on [b]Friday, July 26th![/b]

Season 2 is bringing dozens of changes and additions, including new cosmetics, new challenges, and an all-new season pass to chase. In preparation for next Friday's launch, we've released a massive update today that brings with it many of the core changes and fixes that build the foundation of Season 2.

That also means that this week is the last chance you have to progress the Season 1 Pass and claim any of the exclusive cosmetics included in it! If you haven't dropped in for a while, now is one of the best times to see how far notmycar has come.

In the meantime, you should totally [url=https://discord.gg/notmycar]join our official Discord[/url]. It's the best place to give feedback directly to the NMC team and get support for any issues you may encounter.

With all of that out of the way, on to the patch notes!:

[h1]Game[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Larger Matches[/b] - Now featuring up to 40 players
[*] [b]Faster Matchmaking[/b] - Match quickly, with lowered lobby wait time
[*] [b]World[/b] - World building and Point of Interest updates all across the map; updated lighting and atmospherics
[*] [b]Engine[/b] - Updated to Unreal Engine 4.22
[*] [b]Audio[/b] - FMOD updated to 4.22 
[*] [b]Optimizations[/b] - Continued efforts to optimize performance for best possible gameplay experience
[*] [b]Tutorial[/b] - Updated tutorial to help explain the basic game mechanics for new players
[/list]

[h1]Balance & Tuning[/h1]
[list]
[*] [b]Vehicle Attributes[/b] - Each vehicle now has specific driving characteristics to match your play style; Health, Armor, Braking, Drifting, Acceleration 
[*] [b]Vehicles[/b] - All vehicles drive and react faster - boost is faster overall now, new visual and audio effects added when boosting 
[*] [b]Supply Drop[/b] - Logic adjusted to make landing more accurate
[/list]

The following are known issues with this patch that we're tracking:
[list]
[*] Free aim mode resets between matches (toggle with ALT)
[*] Upon spectating, players may get stuck viewing their own corpse
[*] Placing waypoints to the right of the map moves around all the locations displayed
[*] A white box may appear on the center of map
[*] Supply drops can get stuck when landing on inclines
[*] Green Machine Gun has no reload sound when using Faster Reload 
[*] Rocket Launcher has double reload SFX
[*] Vehicle horns play only in the right channel when in the garage
[*] Inventory menu overrides all player input when activated, including driving controls
[*] Rare Fatal Error crash may occur
[/list]

Thank you for continuing to provide your detailed feedback and bug reports! We can't wait for you to get your hands on Season 2. You can send in feedback and reports directly to the developers in [url=https://discord.gg/notmycar]our official Discord[/url].

<3

notes.title: Regarding Teaming in Solos
notes.content:
A message from NMC Studios:

Hey there, everyone. We have been discussing what to do about the problem with people teaming up in solos quite a bit over the last few days. It's unfortunate that people are doing this, and we realize that it is ruining the experience for many of you, so we have decided to institute a ban on any players who are verified to have been teaming up in solo mode. Here's how it will work:

Anyone suspected of teaming should be reported directly to the #report-players channel in [url=https://discord.gg/notmycar]our official Discord[/url]. Please provide as much info and evidence of teaming as possible - video showing teamers working together with their username clearly identified is ideal. The dev team will review the reports and will make a final determination on whether someone was intentionally teaming up or not. If verified, we will suspend that player's account for 7 days for their first offence and 30 days for their second offence. If a player is found to be teaming a third time, they will be permanently banned from the game.

Players will temporarily see Error Code 14000 if their Steam ID has been banned or suspended. We are going to update this error code so it's more clear to the banned player in a future patch, but for now this generic message will have to do. We will also inform all players that the ban policy is going into effect immediately via the Message of the Day, and will be communicating this info out via our social channels and game FAQ.

If someone believes they were erroneously banned, they can email admin@nmcstudios.com to appeal their suspension.

We are hopeful that this has an immediate impact on the number of players who have been teaming up so we can get back to some good ol' fashioned solo combat. Please know that take this very seriously, as we do not want it to ruin the experience for anyone, especially those of you who have been supporting us by showing up every day.

We are a very small independent development team and are doing everything we can to make the game as fun and fair as possible. Thank you for your continued support as we work through these issues!

notes.title: If you wish battle royale had more honking, your prayers have been answered
notes.content:
I guess we're getting to the point where the battle royale genre is developing its own subgenres. By my count there are already two car-based battle royale games out there—Auto Royale (H1Z1's cars-only mode) and Fractured Lands, the Early Access Mad Max-lookin' BR game—and now they've joined by a third. In other words, if you're looking for a brand new twist on BR, notmycar (yes, all lowercase) might not be it.

This car-based battle royale is free to play so there's no reason not take it for a spin, but it's also in Early Access and there are a lot of issues to be ironed out, especially performance-wise. I've played about a dozen matches since Friday, and here's how it went.

After several minutes of matchmaking and driving around in a lobby, everyone is loaded onto a plane. Since this is a game about cars, everyone spends the entire plane ride honking their horns incessantly. It's incredibly annoying, but then it suddenly becomes kind of hilarious before eventually slipping back into being annoying again. I'm pretty sure it's why most people bail out as soon as possible (there's sound you can turn on in the clip below, if you dare). 

As the plane crosses the map, all the cars jump out and fly to the ground using wings that are attached to the cars. I know this is completely standard in BR, but it seems especially weird to me that a bunch of cars take a ride on an airplane, and then exit the airplane while wearing airplane wings. I think I have some questions about the lore of this world.

Once you land, you start driving around and picking up gear, just like in any other battle royale. This is where notmycar begins to feel even more weird. Maybe I'm used to car games where you pick up stuff by just driving over it, but here you have to aim at an item and click a key to collect it. Sometimes you even have to drive inside buildings like barns and sheds to pick stuff up. It tends to slow everything down to a crawl, which isn't what you'd expect in a vehicle-based game.

There are some cool weapons and abilities to collect, though: rocket launchers, miniguns, sniper rifles, and so on, all which get mounted to the roof of your vehicle. There's also armor, repair kits, EMP blasts, shields, and cloaking devices. It's sort of weird being stealthy in a noisy truck painted lime green, but I managed to pull it off for a while.

I could see notmycar actually being fun—driving around at top speed shooting rockets and miniguns at other cars is easy enough to enjoy. But the biggest problem right now is the poor performance I've been getting. It's just not a very smooth experience, jaggy and laggy to the point of being rather unpleasant and difficult to stomach for more than one or two matches without developing a headache. At high speeds there needs to be a baseline of smoothness and that just wasn't there on any of the matches I played on several different occasions, and it's a common complaint in the Steam reviews.

The other issue besides the lag is all the waiting around you have to do. You wait in a matchmaking menu, then you spend some time loading, then you wait in a lobby, then you spend some time loading, then you wait in a plane, then you spend some time falling, and only then do you actually get to start driving. It's at least a good four or five minutes from when you click to start a match to when you actually begin playing.

I'd hoped after a few years of battle royale, newer games would get you into the action more quickly. If anything, this feels like a step backward. Hopefully this, among other things, will improve while notmycar is in Early Access.

notes.title: Notmycar is doing donuts in early access
notes.content:
Quietly released on Friday, NMC Studios vehicular free-to-play battle royale shooter Notmycar launched into early access. It’s immediately familiar stuff to anyone who has played any other battle royale, only there’s just forty competitors, and it’s somewhat harder for them to hide as they’re all driving around in loud, heavily armed vehicles. After taking it for a spin for a couple rounds, I reckon that so long as this one keeps enough players around, it could grow into something special, but it’s a bit rough around the edges now. Below, a trailer and some thoughts.

notes.title: Official Statement from Turbo Racington, CEO of NMC Studios
notes.content:
I'm excited to announce the Early Access Steam launch of notmycar, a free to play battle royale game entirely with cars! It's notmycar, all one word, all lower case. I'm going to level with you, we spent more time developing the game than the title.

An influencer and an overpaid marketing executive told me to say notmycar is like Rocket League meets Fortnite. I wanted to use "Twisted Metal meets PUBG," but they told me that was, "Dated," and that I was, "Yelling a lot," and to, "Put down the sword." Millennials.

It's free to play and it's the fastest battle royale game on Earth because it's played with cars and cars are faster than people.

Seriously though, its total vehicular mayhem. You’re on a massive island battleground and have to fight for your life at breakneck speeds to outlast the competition and remain the last car standing. Drop, drive and destroy with an arsenal of brutal weapons and abilities. You’ll need a skilled hand on the wheel and the trigger to win too.

Play between April 5th and April 12th and we’ll consider you a “Founder” -  you’ll automagically get a custom paint job for the one-and-only pick-up truck of punishment – The Beast. 

Not sure what else to say except, PLAY! And, NOW! 

- Turbo

notes.title: Notmycar is a vehicular battle royale, coming soon
notes.content:
Notmycar is providing an important service for anyone who has played PUBG and thought "this would be better if we were all cars". Up to 100 cars are dropped onto the battlefield, and they've got to gear up and murder the competition. It sounds as great as the new trailer is obnoxious. And it's pretty obnoxious. 

Since the trailer spends all of its time trying to channel the worst game adverts of the '90s, you'll need to watch last year's teaser if you want to see it in action. 

Also, they're flying cars. Well, gliding cars. That's how they get into the fight—soaring like eagles. Big, metal, heavily-armed eagles. You'll be able to customise your ride with new paint jobs and other cosmetics, as well as beefing it up with weapons and additional equipment. 

It's expected to be in Early Access for six months, during which time driving and combat will be tuned, and more consumables, including weapons, abilities and equipment, will be developed based on player feedback. Early Access will also limit the number of players to 50, which is still a lot of cars, but 1.0 will feature 75+ heavy metal brawls. 

Notmycar will launch on Steam Early Access on April 5 and will be free to play. 

Cheers, RPS.

notes.title: Notmycar is battle royale but with gun-toting cars and a tiresome attitude
notes.content:
“Everything else is just a walking simulator” is just one example of the bug-eyed posturing with which Skybound Games announce Notmycar, their attempt to snaffle a piece of Fort-Legs pie with a free-to-play, automotive-based battle royale.

Notmycar takes the attitude that, if the car-wrecks don’t bring all the boys to the yard, maybe being massively obnoxious will. “Are you tired of the same games day in and day out?”, reads the YouTube blurb. Uh, the whole world says no? Still: I dig the concept.

Skybound Entertainment’s publishing arm Skybound Games today announced a new partnership to bring vehicular battle royale game [b]notmycar[/b]  [url=http://www.notmycar.com/]www.notmycar.com[/url]) to Steam in 2019. [b]notmycar's[/b] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/694720/notmycar/]Steam “coming soon” page[/url] debuts today and includes a [url=http://www.skybound.com/nmccomingsoon]bang-up new trailer[/url].

[b]notmycar [/b]welcomes players to "Test Drive," the game's first-ever closed beta play session this weekend, from noon to midnight PDT on both December 8th and 9th. A select number of test drivers will be notified that they have been chosen to take the game for a spin after signing up at [url=http://notmycar.com/]notmycar.com[/url], which they must do before December 7th at 5pm PDT to participate in this weekend’s Test Drive. [b]notmycar[/b]  drops players onto a massive island battleground where they must outlast the competition to become the last car standing. Players  equip their autos with brutal weapons and abilities to brawl in a vehicular battle royale. To win, players will need more than a tight ride - cunning, skill, and an arsenal of strategy is needed at the wheel to win the fast-paced, chaotic, tire squealing mayhem that is [b]notmycar[/b].  

“Skybound’s constant goal is to create quality content for our fans and new fans alike,” said Skybound Games CEO Ian Howe. “[b]notmycar[/b] is an incredible concept and we’re excited to share this Test Drive with our community. More information relating to the game and its launch will be released in the coming weeks. To follow along and join the [b]notmycar[/b] community, fans should follow the game on [url=https://twitter.com/notmycargame]Twitter[/url].
